caption:
Another week, another talent tracker. Names move into corner offices. Yours isn't on the list again.

Read that list differently this week. Don't ask whether those leaders were more capable than you. Ask what the room believed about them before the decision was made.

Elevation is rarely a verdict on competence. It's a verdict on what the senior room had already concluded about your command presence — long before the shortlist existed. Who carries weight when they walk in. Whose pause makes people wait. Whose voice doesn't climb under pressure.

Colonel Suhag spent 35 years in military command watching that judgment form in seconds. It forms the same way in a boardroom.

Resentment is a dead end. Diagnosis isn't. Take one name off this week's list and work out precisely what the room saw in them that it does not yet see in you. Then fix that.

topic.title: Weekly leadership churn: who got the corner office
topic.angle: Qualified-but-overlooked professionals read a list of elevated names every week that never includes theirs, so dissecting what the room believed about those leaders turns resentment into a diagnostic about command presence rather than competence.
topic.why_now: BestMediaInfo's recurring weekly 'Talent tracker' published a fresh edition within the last six days and Business Standard's India business leaders section updated within the last day, making this a structurally repeatable Monday/Tuesday slot.

rationale: A stark text-only card matches the no-nonsense command tone and keeps the weekly leadership-list diagnostic as the single focal idea.
